title: Central collection of patient data and biomaterial bank for aplastic anaemia and bone marrow failure syndromes
summary:
The group of aplastic syndromes is a rare disease characterised by a lack of blood formation with the symptoms of bi- or tricytopenia with anaemia, granulocytopenia and thrombocytopenia in various combinations and to varying degrees. Overall, this group consists of a large number of different syndromes, from which large groups can be distinguished. One is the group of aplastic syndromes and the other is the group of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes, of which telomeropathies make up the largest proportion.
Systematic recording in a disease-specific registry is particularly necessary for rare diseases in order to enable representative statements to be made about risk factors, prognostic variables and therapy-associated outcomes. In the group of telomeropathies in particular, there was no epidemiological data on the manifestations of the disease, its course or possible therapeutic approaches until the introduction of the telomeropathy register.
conditions: (Suspected) aplastic anaemia; congenital aplastic syndrome; congenital syndrome assosiated with cytopenia; bone marrow failure; unclear cytopenia, telomeropathy

interventions.name: In this registry, clinical data (symptoms, laboratory parameters, etc.) of patients with: aplastic anemia; congenital aplastic syndrome; congenital syndrome associated with cytopenia or unclear cytopenia are documented. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients suspected of having aplastic anaemia, a congenital aplastic syndrome, a congenital syndrome associated with cytopenias or an unclear cytopenia and blood is sent to the registry centre in Aachen for telomere length determination and, if necessary, genetic diagnostics.
Consent to the registry, biobanking and transmission of blood for telomere length determination and, if necessary, genetic diagnostics to the registry center in Aachen.
Exclusion criteria:
No exclusion criteria are explicitly formulated. In particular, patients with comorbidities and a non-curative intended therapy can be explicitly included in order to generate a picture of the reality of care.
